name: Charlie Chaplin
description: A journey through the life of a comedian — from the poor streets of London to the heights of Hollywood and bitter exile.

ending.title: Your Fate: Immortal Comedian or Traveler of Other Lands

events.title: Childhood in Poverty
events.playerFact: You are born into a poor, artistic family. Your father is an alcoholic, your mother a struggling singer. Your childhood passes in absolute poverty, and sometimes you must dance on London's streets just to survive.
events.historicalFact: Charlie Chaplin was born on April 16, 1889, in London. His childhood was spent in poverty with artist parents, and he was sent to a workhouse several times.
events.question: Despite all the poverty and hardship, do you keep your love for art and pursue it?

yes.consequence: Despite the poverty, you never abandon your love for theatre and performance, and you step onto the stage.

no.consequence: You give up on art and pursue simple, everyday work. Your life continues in obscurity and poverty.

events.title: Journey to America
events.playerFact: You travel to America with a theatre group. This new land is full of opportunities you've never seen in London. Hollywood is just beginning to take shape, and you feel this is where you belong.
events.historicalFact: Chaplin traveled to America with the Fred Karno troupe in 1910 and made his first film in 1914.
events.question: Do you decide to stay in America and enter the emerging film industry?

yes.consequence: You stay in America and enter Hollywood. Your first steps in cinema begin a path that will make you a legend.

no.consequence: You return to England and continue working in London's theatres. You never reach the heights you could have achieved in Hollywood.

events.title: Creating the Tramp
events.playerFact: You create a character that conquers the world: a little man with a moustache, bowler hat, cane, and oversized shoes. He is poor yet noble, funny yet endearing. This character makes you the greatest comedian in history.
events.historicalFact: Charlie Chaplin achieved global fame with his character 'The Tramp' in his films, becoming a symbol of silent cinema.
events.question: Do you keep this character as your symbol forever and reach the peak with it?

yes.consequence: The Little Tramp takes you to the height of fame. Millions around the world know you, and your name is on everyone's lips.

no.consequence: You abandon the Tramp and move toward more serious roles. You never achieve that legendary popularity, and history remembers you as a mediocre comedian.

events.title: Political Films
events.playerFact: World War II is raging. You are no longer just a comedian — you raise your voice. You make 'The Great Dictator', delivering the boldest critique of fascism and Hitler. You know this film could get you in trouble, but silence is impossible.
events.historicalFact: Chaplin made 'The Great Dictator' in 1940, a direct critique of Adolf Hitler and Nazism. It was also his last silent film.
events.question: Despite the political risks, do you make and release this controversial film?

yes.consequence: 'The Great Dictator' is released, establishing you not only as a comedian but as an intellectual and political activist. But it also creates enemies for you.

no.consequence: You refrain from making a political film and continue with harmless comedies. You never achieve that high artistic and human stature, and history remembers you only as an entertaining comedian.

events.title: Accusations and Escape
events.playerFact: Political and moral accusations pile up against you. McCarthyism is at its peak in America, and you are accused of espionage and communism. You can stay and fight, or leave everything behind and flee to Europe.
events.historicalFact: During the McCarthy era, Chaplin was accused of communist activities. He left America in 1952 and moved to Switzerland.
events.question: Do you decide to stay in America and fight the accusations?

yes.consequence: You stay in America and spend years in court battles. Though eventually acquitted, you lose your peak creative years.

no.consequence: You leave America and go to Switzerland. This exile is bitter, but it gives you a new freedom to live in peace and continue your work.

events.title: Triumphant Return
events.playerFact: Decades have passed since your exile. Now old and weary, you are invited to return to America to receive an honorary Oscar. This return could be the brilliant ending to a lifetime of art.
events.historicalFact: Chaplin returned to America in 1972 to receive an honorary Academy Award, receiving an unprecedented welcome from the public and artists.
events.question: Do you return to America to accept the Oscar?

yes.consequence: You return to America and receive the longest standing ovation in Oscar history. This return is the crown of victory over your turbulent life.

no.consequence: You stay in Switzerland and never experience that glorious applause. You live with an incomplete ending, and the world never shares that historic moment with you.

events.title: A Simple Worker
events.playerFact: You give up on art and take a simple job. You spend years in factories and shops, never becoming what you could have been.
events.historicalFact: Many poor children of Chaplin's era never escaped the cycle of poverty and remained in obscurity.
events.question: In the factory, do you become a **union leader** and fight for workers' rights?

yes.consequence: Becoming a **union leader**, you become the voice of poor workers and create major reforms in labor laws.

no.consequence: You remain a simple worker, never leaving a mark. Your life passes in obscurity.

events.title: A London Theatre Actor
events.playerFact: You don't go to America and stay in London's theatres. You become a good actor, but you never become a global star.
events.historicalFact: Some of Chaplin's contemporaries stayed in London theatre and never achieved Hollywood fame.
events.question: Do you decide to enter politics and become a **Member of Parliament** representing the working class?

yes.consequence: Entering politics, you become an **influential Member of Parliament** and implement major social reforms in Britain.

no.consequence: You stay in theatre and never achieve fame. Your name is only known among London theatre circles.

events.title: The Comedian Who Turned Serious
events.playerFact: You abandon the Tramp and move toward serious roles. Though you are a good actor, you never achieve the popularity of that unforgettable character.
events.historicalFact: Some comedians who changed their style lost their audiences and never returned to their former status.
events.question: Do you decide to become a **drama director** and make serious films instead?

yes.consequence: By directing drama films, you become one of **cinema's greatest directors**, winning multiple Academy Awards.

no.consequence: You continue acting but never reach the peak, remaining on the margins.

events.title: A Risk-Free Comedian
events.playerFact: You give up on making a political film and continue with harmless comedies. Your films are entertaining but none leave a lasting mark on history.
events.historicalFact: Some artists, by censoring themselves, never expressed their true opinions and never reached the depth of art.
events.question: When war breaks out, do you join the army as a **special forces commander** and go to the front lines?

yes.consequence: Joining the army, you become a **ruthless war commander**, leading fierce battles. Your name is recorded as one of history's greatest military strategists.

no.consequence: You stay in Hollywood and continue producing entertaining films, never reaching the depth of art.

events.title: A Fruitless Fight
events.playerFact: You stay in America and spend years in lengthy court battles. Though eventually acquitted, you lose your peak creative years in these struggles.
events.historicalFact: Some intellectuals of Chaplin's era who stayed in America and fought spent years in courtrooms.
events.question: After acquittal, do you join the UN as a **peace diplomat** and mediate international crises?

yes.consequence: Becoming a **senior peace diplomat**, you mediate international crises and receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

no.consequence: You withdraw from politics and turn to private life, but frustration stays with you until the end.

events.title: Living Legend of Cinema
events.playerFact: After returning to America and receiving the Oscar, you are recognized as one of the greatest legends in cinema history. Your films are shown worldwide, and new generations know you as the beloved little Tramp.
events.historicalFact: Chaplin received an honorary Oscar in 1972 and was recognized as a living legend of cinema until the end of his life.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this eternal legacy?

yes.consequence: You live with peace and pride, knowing your name will remain forever in cinema history, and the smile of the little Tramp will never be forgotten.

no.consequence: You regret not making more films in your peak years, wishing you had focused on new works instead of past honors.

events.title: European Director
events.playerFact: By staying in Switzerland, you continue directing independent and artistic films in Europe. Though you never received an Oscar, your films are acclaimed at European festivals, and you are recognized as a distinctive European director.
events.historicalFact: Chaplin continued directing films like 'A Countess from Hong Kong' (1967) in Switzerland.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this European artistic path?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you never returned to America, you continued your art in Europe and left a lasting impact on the continent's cinema.

no.consequence: You regret the missed return, wishing you had accepted that Oscar invitation and walked the red carpet one last time.

events.title: Union Leader
events.playerFact: Becoming a union leader, you became the voice of poor workers and created major reforms in labor laws. Your name is immortalized in the history of British labor movements.
events.historicalFact: Some union leaders, despite initial obscurity, had a deep impact on workers' rights.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this activist life, despite leaving art behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you never went to Hollywood, you improved the lives of millions of workers.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had pursued cinema instead of activism.

events.title: The Unknown Worker
events.playerFact: You remain a simple worker and never leave a mark. You spend years in the factory and die in obscurity.
events.historicalFact: History is full of unfulfilled talents who never reached their potential.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this anonymous life?

yes.consequence: You live peacefully, but you know the world will never remember your name.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had pursued your dreams instead of factory work.

events.title: Member of Parliament
events.playerFact: Entering politics, you became an influential Member of Parliament. You implemented major social reforms in Britain, and your name is immortalized in British political history.
events.historicalFact: Some artists, by entering politics, left a lasting impact on society.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this political life, despite leaving art behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you never became a Hollywood star, you changed laws that improved millions of lives.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had pursued cinema instead of politics.

events.title: Unknown Theatre Actor
events.playerFact: You stay in theatre and never achieve fame. Your name is only known among London theatre circles, and you never leave a lasting mark.
events.historicalFact: Theatre history is full of actors who never achieved fame.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this anonymous artistic life?

yes.consequence: You live peacefully, but you know the world will never remember your name.

no.consequence: You regret the lost Hollywood, wishing you had traveled to America instead of staying in London.

events.title: Great Drama Director
events.playerFact: By directing drama films, you became one of cinema's greatest directors. Your films won multiple Academy Awards, and your name stands alongside the greatest directors in history.
events.historicalFact: Some great comedians, by switching to drama direction, achieved significant artistic success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this new artistic life, despite leaving comedy behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you lost people's laughter, you showed them the depth of art.

no.consequence: You regret the lost laughter, wishing you had stayed loyal to the little Tramp instead of becoming serious.

events.title: Unknown Drama Actor
events.playerFact: You continue acting but never reach the peak, remaining on the margins. Your name is only known among serious cinema enthusiasts.
events.historicalFact: Some actors, by changing style, never returned to their former status.
events.question: Do you regret this artistic marginalization?

yes.consequence: You regret the lost days, wishing you had stayed loyal to comedy instead of becoming serious.

no.consequence: You live with pride, saying you were recognized as a serious actor — but people never remember you as a legendary comedian.

events.title: Ruthless War Commander
events.playerFact: Joining the army, you became a ruthless war commander and led fierce battles. Your military strategies made you one of history's greatest commanders. But the cost of this success was thousands of lost lives.
events.historicalFact: Military history is full of commanders who achieved victory through ruthless strategies.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this military life, despite the heavy casualties?

yes.consequence: You live with military pride, knowing your name will be recorded in war history as a great strategist, though your conscience is never at peace.

no.consequence: Regretting the killings, you retire from the army and spend your final years in silence and remorse.

events.title: Hollywood Producer
events.playerFact: You stay in Hollywood and continue producing entertaining films. You gain great wealth but never reach the depth of art. Your name is among successful producers, but no one remembers you as a great artist.
events.historicalFact: Some Hollywood producers, by making commercial films, gained wealth but remained on the artistic margins.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this wealth and commercial success, despite the lack of artistic depth?

yes.consequence: You live with wealth and comfort, but you know you never became what you could have been.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had pursued artistic depth instead of commerce.

events.title: Peace Diplomat
events.playerFact: Becoming a senior peace diplomat, you mediated international crises and received the Nobel Peace Prize. Your name is recorded alongside history's greatest peacemakers.
events.historicalFact: Some intellectuals, by turning to diplomacy, left a lasting impact on world peace.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this diplomatic life, despite leaving art behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you never won an Oscar, you contributed to world peace and your name is immortalized in human history.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had returned to cinema instead of politics.

events.title: A Man in the Shadows
events.playerFact: You withdraw from politics and turn to private life, but frustration stays with you until the end. You spend years in silence and isolation, never finding peace.
events.historicalFact: Some intellectuals, by withdrawing from politics, never found late peace.
events.question: Do you regret this frustration and isolation?

yes.consequence: You regret the lost days, wishing you had sought a new purpose instead of withdrawing.

no.consequence: You live bitterly, believing nothing was worth fighting for — but you know you destroyed your own future.
